'''Javier Sánchez Vicario''' ({{IPA|es|xaˈβjeɾ ˈsantʃeθ}}; born 1 February 1968) is a former top-ten doubles professional [[tennis]] player from Spain. Sánchez won the [[1986 US Open (tennis)|US Open]] junior singles and doubles title in 1986, and reached the quarterfinal stage in the [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]] men's singles event twice – in 1991 and 1996.

==Career==
{{BLP sources section|date=February 2024}}
Sánchez won the [[1986 US Open (tennis)|US Open]] junior singles and doubles title in 1986, partnering with [[Tomás Carbonell (tennis)|Tomás Carbonell]], and became world no. 1 junior that same year.<ref name="Junior">{{cite news | title=ATP Javier Sanchez Bio | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/javier-sanchez/s015/bio |access-date=18 July 2020 | work=ATP Website}}</ref>

In Javier's first career singles final in 1987 in [[Madrid Tennis Grand Prix|Madrid]], he faced his brother [[Emilio Sánchez]]. Emilio won the match in three sets. Emilio and Javier would play each other a total of 12 times during their careers, Emilio winning ten of their encounters and Javier winning two. They also partnered together to win three doubles titles.

Sanchez won his first professional doubles titles in 1987 and his first singles title in 1988 in [[1988 Buenos Aires Grand Prix – Singles|Buenos Aires]]. His best grand slam performances included reaching the quarterfinals of the US Open in 1991 (defeating world no. 5 [[Sergi Bruguera]]) and 1996. Sanchez also reached the semifinals of the [[1994 ATP German Open – Singles|1994 Hamburg Masters]]. He won a career total of four singles titles and 26 doubles titles, and reached a career-high ranking of no. 23 in singles (in 1994) and no. 9 in doubles (in 1992).

==Personal life==
Sánchez is a member of one of the world's most successful tennis families. His younger sister [[Arantxa Sánchez Vicario]] achieved the world no. 1 ranking in both singles and doubles, and won four [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] singles titles; and his older brother [[Emilio Sánchez]] reached world no. 1 in doubles and won five Grand Slam doubles titles. They also have an older sister – Marisa – who also played professional tennis, peaking at world no. 368 in 1990.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}}

Sánchez and wife Isabel wed in September 1994. They have two daughters, Alba (born July 1998) and Julia (born March 2000).<ref name="Junior"/>

In 2012, Arantxa Sánchez Vicario sued Javier Sánchez (and their father) for the alleged mishandling and embezzlement of her $60 million career earnings. The court case continued over three years, and in 2015 concluded in a private settlement.<ref name="Sue">{{cite news | last1=Lynch |first1=Donal | title=Game, set and... cash troubles: how Wimbledon stars like Becker, Borg and Sanchez courted controversies | url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/life/weekend/game-set-and-cash-troubles-how-wimbledon-stars-like-becker-borg-and-sanchez-courted-controversies-37055915.html |access-date=18 July 2020 | work=Belfast Telegraph| date=30 June 2018}}</ref>
